empirical_tests: E0 Preregistration and infrastructure. Register on OSF and, preferably, submit a Registered Report Stage 1 to Royal Society Open Science. RSOS covers all science, engineering and mathematics and has offered RRs since 2015 [V]; its policy for physics RRs specifically is unverified [U]. Freeze before data download: Rule R, the gates, the estimators (MLE/Hill above s_e; Gabaix-Ibragimov rank-1/2 OLS as secondary [V]), the tolerances, the system list and the power analysis. Hash the predictions before the held-out fitting code runs. Extend the repo's run_gibrat.py and tests/test_gibrat.py to check the exact profile and the finite-age front; the scratchpad prototypes are profile_check.py and front_check.py.

E1 Pipeline validation, explicitly not evidence. Reproduce Zhang & Sornette 2011 (0.75 ± 0.05) and Hisano et al. 2011 from their published rates using src/orthopolity.gibrat_zeta. Recover simulated zeta across phi in [-0.02, 0.05]; results/gibrat.json already does this [R]. Run parameter-recovery simulations at the sample sizes and panel lengths of each real system to calibrate gate thresholds and power.

E2 Primary held-out test A: algorithmically defined urban centres. Data: GHS-UCDB R2024A, multitemporal delineation, about 11,000 centres, epochs 1975-2020 [V]. Use observed epochs only and exclude the 2025/2030 projections; per-epoch field names are unverified [U]. Design: unit = centre, resource = resident population, system = country (with a preregistered minimum tail count). Estimate mu, sigma^2, h (disappearance or merger), nu and s_e from 1975-2000; predict zeta and the B(u) slope for 2020. Score with the errors-in-variables calibration regression across countries. Known weaknesses, stated in advance: GHS-POP is disaggregated from censuses, so growth variance is partly modelled; centres merge (a coagulation term); and relaxation is slow, so the R6 relaxation gate may exclude many countries. If so, report it as a scope result.

E3 Primary held-out test B: US firms from public Census BDS. (i) Age test: compute each birth cohort's employment relative to the entry flow as a function of age to estimate phi directly. The theorem predicts employment per unit age ∝ e^(-phi a) [D]. (ii) Size test: use employment shares by firm-size class to estimate the B(u) slope. (iii) Prediction: zeta - 1 from phi and m, with sigma^2 either taken from published LBD-based estimates or calibrated as one nuisance parameter on a random half of sector×state systems and tested on the other half. Exact BDS cross-tab availability (firm age × firm size × sector × state) must be confirmed [U].

E4 Primary held-out test C: US-listed firms from SEC EDGAR XBRL financial-statement datasets (2009-present) [U for the exact coverage of the public files]. Resources = total assets and revenue, both analysed per R3. Estimate rates 2010-2017; predict the 2024 cross-section. Entry = first filing, exit = last filing. Report financial and non-financial firms separately, as preregistered.

E5 Deviation-calculus test where O_log is NOT predicted: BCI forest. Data: 8 censuses 1982-2015, Dryad doi:10.15146/5xcp-0d46 [V]. Resource = aboveground biomass via a preregistered allometry (e.g., Chave et al. 2014 [U]). Estimate g(M), h(M), sigma^2(M) and recruitment from 1982-2005; predict the local biomass-per-log-mass slope in 2010 and 2015. Success means predicting zeta < 1 correctly. This guards against a theory that only ever predicts 1. Cite Muller-Landau et al. 2006 as prior art for demographic-equilibrium prediction [V].

E6 Prospective test, the only fully blind one. Pick an open system with a unit-held additive stock and a public API, for example user accounts per fediverse server [U for data access]. Measure rates for 6 months, publish the predicted zeta and front position, and test at 12 and 24 months. Systems with fast turnover are preferred because they relax faster.

E7 Sign-rule meta-test with outcomes coded blind. Using only documented entry/exit facts, code the sign of phi for literature systems before their zeta is looked up, then score agreement. Known calibration entries [V]: Amazee (phi < 0, zeta 0.75); US administrative places with incorporation entry (zeta 1.3-1.4, Clauset 2009; Malevergne-Pisarenko-Sornette); CCA clusters (≈1, Rozenfeld 2011); US firms (1.06-1.10); mutual funds (lognormal, unrelaxed). Exclude systems whose tail is not power-law by a lognormal LR test.

E8 Out-of-domain controls under Rule R, to report the domain boundary without claiming it. USGS moment zeta_M0 = 0.666 [R]; GCMT beta 0.60-0.65 [V]; flare energies alpha_E ≈ 1.5-1.8 [V]. Keep the existing repo pipelines; relabel the area and fluence analyses as the 'loophole demonstration' in the SI.

E9 Power and estimation. SE(Hill zeta) ≈ zeta/sqrt(n_tail), so resolving |zeta - 1| = 0.05 at 95% needs n_tail ≳ 1,600 per system [D arithmetic]. The prediction needs SE(phi) ≤ 0.025 m. Systems below these thresholds enter only the pooled calibration regression with their errors. Use calendar-block bootstrap for temporal dependence and region-block bootstrap for spatial dependence. Run a lognormal and double-Pareto-lognormal likelihood-ratio test for every tail.
falsification_criteria: F1 Calibration of the deviation law. Over all systems passing the R6 gates, regress (zeta_obs - 1) on (zeta_pred - 1) with errors in variables. The law is falsified if the slope's 95% CI excludes 1 or the intercept's excludes 0.

F2 Skill against nulls. The out-of-sample MSE of zeta_pred must be lower than that of BOTH null predictors: zeta ≡ 1 and zeta ≡ the training-window cross-system mean. The block-bootstrap CI of the skill score must exclude 0. Skill ≤ 0 means the theory adds nothing, even if zeta clusters near 1.

F3 Fixed point. A gated, relaxed system whose measured |phi|/m has an upper 95% bound ≤ 0.02 but whose zeta_obs 95% CI excludes the band implied by phi's CI (about 1 ± 0.05) falsifies 'O_log ⟺ phi = 0'.
F4 Sign rule. A gated, relaxed system with phi significantly > 0 and zeta significantly < 1, or phi significantly < 0 and zeta significantly > 1, within the fitted range below any named cutoff.

F5 Profile shape. Theorem B predicts an exactly exponential B(u) above s_e. Significant curvature in B(u) above s_e (preregistered quadratic-term test) in a system passing the Gibrat gate falsifies the exact-profile claim. So does a plateau extending beyond (mu + sigma^2/2)T + 3 sigma sqrt(T), or ending before mT - 3 sigma sqrt(T).
F6 Age-size consistency (BDS-type data). phi estimated from the cohort-age profile and phi implied by the size-profile slope differ by more than their combined uncertainty.

F7 Mechanism specificity. If zeta_obs ≈ 1 is as frequent among gated systems with large |phi|/m as among those with phi ≈ 0 (no association between zeta and phi), the claimed mechanism is falsified even if zeta clusters near 1. Seeing zeta ≈ 1 alone is never counted as support.

F8 Domain tally, which limits scope rather than falsifying. If fewer than a preregistered fraction (e.g., one third) of candidate systems pass the gates, the abstract must say the theorem covers a minority of examined systems. Gate failures and out-of-domain controls (event catalogs, cascades) never count as support. Their non-1 exponents count against any claim of generality beyond the stated class.

F9 Resource loophole audit. If any admissible resource under R3 (e.g., firm assets vs employment) fails F1 to F4 while another passes, the failure is reported with equal prominence and counts in the tally. Post hoc resources (rupture area, band fluence) are never counted.
design.what_to_drop:
KEEP and promote
- Repo paper §2.1-2.2 (accounting identity, measure dependence, the linear-vs-log table) and §2.3 (conservation does not select a shape; the vacuity lemma 'resource must not be fitted'; the exponential-cost non-power example). These motivate Rule R and Part A.
- src/orthopolity.gibrat_zeta, experiments/run_gibrat.py, tests/test_gibrat.py and results/gibrat.json. These are the core numerical validation. Add the exact-profile and finite-age-front checks; prototypes are in the scratchpad profile_check.py and front_check.py.
- results/resource_choice.json, moved to the SI as an explicit 'loophole demonstration'. It shows that the same catalogue gives zeta = 0.998 (area proxy) vs 0.666 (moment), and fluence alpha = 2.13 vs 1.90 depending on background handling, which is why Rule R is needed.
- The earthquake and flare pipelines, kept as out-of-domain controls with the rule-designated resource. Report moment zeta_M0 = 0.666 [0.649, 0.683] [R].
- The Hatton ocean re-expression (slope -0.039 [-0.058, -0.026]) [R], in the SI as consistency with existing size-spectrum theory (n - q ≈ -0.05) [V]. It is not orthopolity evidence.
- The source audit and checksum/reproducibility infrastructure, kept internally.

DROP from the main argument
- Any claim of a natural, cosmological or universal law. The 'Orthopolity cosmological principle' and all spacetime, dark-matter and bits-to-energy material.
- The 2017 linear-allocation version. Mention it in one sentence: it corresponds to linear-measure equipartition and Benford sum-invariance (Allaart 1997) [V], and is not predicted by the dynamics.
- Rupture-area O_log and GOES-fluence alpha ≈ 2 as supporting evidence. Both fail Rule R. Area is also anticipated by Aki's D = 2b [V], and fluence by Hudson's criterion [V].
- GLOSSAQUA compatibility fractions, the ensemble/median-slope arguments (§2.4, §4.4-4.5), and the variance, strata and latent-distribution analyses. Reasons: metadata defects (377 StudyID_07 records), two studies supply 78% of slopes, currency and binning artifacts of about 0.1 in slope [V], and no rates to test a mechanism.
  - At most, keep one SI paragraph and the cosh lemma as a statistical caution.
  - The median -1.015 is NOT evidence for the dynamical law.
- MaxEnt or Haar 'derivations' presented as support. Keep them only as the negative result in theory item T2.
- Resource-weighted Benford. It is correct [D] but statistically weak: its Fisher information on the tilt is about 1/M^2 of a direct slope fit.
- The sonification, the viewer and 'friction' language.
- The independent-inputs exponent-addition argument (repo counterexample).
- Social and normative conclusions.

REWRITE
- The introduction: from 'orthopolity as a resource-allocation hypothesis' to 'when does conservative scale-free transport allocate equal resource per scale, and do measured imbalances predict the deviations?'
- The discussion of the authors' intuition. 'Nature doesn't care about concentration' becomes Gibrat scale-invariance of the log-speed; 'conservation' becomes lossless flux and cohort conservation; 'constraints cause deviations' becomes the measured terms phi and d ln v/du.
biggest_risks: Novelty. The exponent equation, the zeta = 1 balance condition and single-domain zero-parameter tests are already published (Reed 2001; SMS 2010; MSS 2013; Luttmer 2007; Zhang-Sornette 2011; Hisano et al. 2011) [V]. A referee will call the theory a rediscovery unless the paper (a) attributes all of it, (b) makes the preregistered multi-domain test the contribution, and (c) confirms that N2-N5 are not in Reed, SMS or GLLM. Full texts could not be read in this session.

Gibrat gates may fail in most real systems, shrinking the domain. Firm volatility scales as sigma ∝ S^-0.2 [V]; city growth variance falls with size (Rozenfeld et al. 2008 PNAS 105:18702) [V]; Bitcoin wealth shows sublinear preferential attachment and a stretched-exponential distribution (Kondor et al. 2014) [V]. The local formula then needs size-resolved rates and more data, and power drops.

Non-stationarity and slow relaxation. Cities relax over centuries if sigma^2 is small. Mutual-fund tails stay lognormal because relaxation is extremely slow (Schwarzkopf-Farmer 2010) [V], and GLLM 2016 show slow tail transitions [V]. Observed zeta may reflect history rather than current rates. The relaxation gate may exclude the most famous Zipf systems.

Low power and noisy inputs. zeta - 1 ≈ phi/m is a ratio of small, noisy rates. Prediction CIs may be too wide to separate the theory from the null zeta ≡ 1, and tails need n_tail ≳ 1,600 per system [D]. The test can then end up uninformative rather than confirming.

Data access and quality. All-firm and product microdata are confidential (LBD, Orbis, POS). GHS-POP populations are model-disaggregated, so their growth variance is partly modelled. The BDS cross-tabs, EDGAR XBRL coverage and fediverse API access are unverified [U]. BCI terms may request co-authorship [V].

Unit definition and coherence. The exponent depends on how units are defined (administrative places 1.3-1.4 vs CCA clusters ≈1) [V]. Mergers act as coagulation. Cristelli et al. and De Marzo et al. show zeta = 1 is not additive across subsystems [V]. Choosing 'country' as the system is itself a modelling choice.

Mechanism non-identifiability. Sample-space-reducing processes, latent-variable mixtures, criticality and Fisher-information principles also give zeta ≈ 1 [V]. Only the measured phi-zeta association (F7) identifies the mechanism, and it may be weak.

Scope conflict with the authors. Under Rule R, the authors' showcase cases (earthquake area, flare fluence, the GLOSSAQUA median) lose evidential status. Event catalogs and many stocks are explicit counterexamples to generality: moment 0.63-0.67, flare energy 0.5-0.8, IMF, galaxy stellar mass, wildfires, trees [V/R]. The authors may reject the narrower, conditional claim, and a broader claim would not survive review.

Garden of forking paths. Gate thresholds, s_e, the allometry, the system list and the choice of admissible resources all have to be frozen before data access. Any later change converts the study back into exploratory analysis, as already happened with the repo's 2026-09-09 plan (local commit order only, not a public registration).

Finite-N effects. Near zeta = 1 the largest unit holds a share of the total that shrinks only logarithmically with system size, and the limits N → ∞ and c → 0 do not commute (Malcai et al. 1999) [V]. Single-system tails will fluctuate strongly at the top, which inflates F5 false alarms unless finite-N corrections are simulated.
design.title_and_venue_options:
TITLES
1. 'Equal resource per scale as the fixed point of conservative proportional growth: a parameter-free, preregistered test across systems'.
2. 'Orthopolity: when scale-free transport allocates equal resource per logarithmic size, and why it usually does not'.
3. 'Flux over speed: a conservation account of Zipf-like resource allocation and its measured deviations'.
4. For an ecology-only spin-off: 'Demographic budgets predict forest biomass size spectra: a resource-variable test'.
Avoid 'natural law', 'universal' and 'cosmological' in titles.

VENUES, in order of realism
1. Royal Society Open Science as a Registered Report. Stage 1 in-principle acceptance before data, which neutralizes the post hoc concern. RSOS covers all of science and mathematics and has offered RRs since 2015 [V]; physics-specific RR handling is unverified [U].
2. Physical Review E (statistical and nonlinear physics). This is the right home for Theorem B plus the multi-domain test. Hisano et al. 2011 [V] and Malevergne-Pisarenko-Sornette appeared in PRE, so the topic fits.
3. Physical Review Research or J. Stat. Mech., for the theory with modest data.
4. PNAS. Only if E2-E4 plus E6 succeed in at least 3-4 domains, with positive skill over nulls and a clean (zeta_obs - 1) vs (zeta_pred - 1) data collapse that includes a predicted zeta < 1 case.
5. PRL. Only for a striking zero-parameter collapse across domains, ideally with the prospective test E6 confirmed. It is high risk given the prior art; do not target it first.
6. Ecology Letters or American Naturalist, for the forest/size-spectrum deviation test as a separate paper, with prior art front-loaded.

SEQUENCING
(a) Theory note plus Rule R plus simulations, as a preprint and the RR Stage 1.
(b) Data analyses on frozen predictions.
(c) Prospective follow-up.
Authorship and AI-assistance disclosures need agreement first. Per the repo roadmap, do not copy the 2017 declarations.

referee.verdict_if_submitted_as_designed: REJECT for PRL. The design does not support the authors' central claim that orthopolity is a general property of real systems. Under its own Rule R it shows the opposite: every system outside the Gibrat stock class is non-O_log. These include seismic moment zeta_M0 = 0.666 [R], flare energy 0.5-0.8 [V], cascades 5/6 [V], the IMF [V], galaxy stellar mass about 0.47 [V] and forests [V]. Inside the class, the claim reduces to the Reed (2001) / Saichev-Malevergne-Sornette exponent equation, which is already published [V]. Within that class, zeta = 1 is not a fixed point: it is a limit that no stationary system reaches (see fatal problem 2). A large part of the proposed 'zero-parameter prediction' follows from accounting identities and is not a test of a dynamical law. The candidate novelties N2-N5 are, respectively, Reed's double-Pareto result, Reed's exponential-age mechanism, the McKendrick-von Foerster / Platt-Denman / Kolmogorov flux closure, and a finite-time front in the spirit of Gabaix-Lasry-Lions-Moll (2016). Statistical power with the systems likely to pass the gates is low. Fairness requires saying that this is the most honest version of the project I have seen. Rule R, the vacuity lemma, the skill-versus-null criterion F2 and the mechanism-specificity criterion F7 are exactly right. As a Registered Report in PRE or RSOS, after the changes below, it could be a solid paper. It is not a PRL paper, and it is not evidence for a natural law.
fatal_problems: F-1. The design gives up the claim it is supposed to support. The authors want 'orthopolity is a general property of real systems'. The design keeps O_log only for a class defined as the set of systems where the Reed/SMS theorem applies (Gibrat growth, size-independent hazard, entry at the bottom, relaxed). Everything else is labelled 'out of domain', and there the paper's own numbers contradict O_log: seismic moment 0.666 [0.649, 0.683] [R]; GCMT beta 0.60-0.65 (Kagan 2002) [V]; flare energy alpha_E about 1.5-1.8 [V]; Dohnanyi 5/6 [V]; galaxy stellar mass about 0.47 (Baldry 2012) [V]; the IMF (Kroupa 2001) [V]; tropical-cyclone PDI, rain and wildfires well below 1 [V]; Clauset 2009's 24 datasets centred near 1.3 [V, dossier]. Restricting generality to the domain where a known theorem guarantees the result is not generality; it is the theorem. Submitted under the authors' framing, the paper refutes itself.

F-2. Within the domain, O_log is a limit that no stationary system reaches, not a fixed point. The resource budget gives dQ/dt = (mu - h)Q + J_R. Stationarity relative to an entry flow growing at nu then gives phi = h + nu - mu = J_R/Q exactly [D]. Check: for Reed's double Pareto (GBM started at s_e and observed at an exponential age with rate lambda = h + nu), E[S] = s_e*lambda/(lambda - mu), so J_R/Q = lambda*s_e/E[S] = lambda - mu = phi [D, standard]. Consequences:
- (a) For any stationary system with positive entry, phi > 0 strictly, so Theorem B predicts zeta > 1 strictly. zeta = 1 is the infimum, reached only as Q/J_R -> infinity. This is the same structure as Gabaix's 1/(1 - s_min/sbar) [V], Visser's z > 1 [V], Malcai-Biham-Solomon's non-commuting limits [V] and the Blank-Solomon (2000) criticism [V].
- (b) The phi < 0 branch of the sign rule (zeta < 1) needs a total dominated by the advancing front, so it cannot pass the R6 relaxation gate. F4 is therefore half-vacuous, and within the gated class every predicted 'deviation' has the same sign.
- (c) zeta - 1 ≈ phi/m = 1/(m*tau_res), with tau_res = Q/J_R the mean resource residence time. 'O_log' then just means 'resource travels many e-folds in log-size before leaving': old, slow-turnover systems. That is a restatement of Gabaix, not a law of allocation.
The precise statement 'O_log <=> phi = 0' should be replaced with 'zeta -> 1+ as phi/m -> 0+, and phi = J_R/Q > 0 in every stationary system'. Once it is, the physics claim of a fixed point is gone.

F-3. Novelty falls below the PRL bar, and the candidate novelties are already in the literature.
- N2, the exact (not asymptotic) exponential B(u) above the entry size: this is Reed's double-Pareto result. A GBM observed at an exponentially distributed age has an exact piecewise power-law density, with exponents given by the roots of the same quadratic. See Reed 2001, Econ. Lett. 74(1):15-19 [V via secondary sources], and Reed & Hughes 2002, PRE 66:067103, which states the 'killed exponential growth' mechanism generally [V]. The resource-weighted version is a one-line size-bias of the same density.
- N3, the cohort-age equivalence: the exponential age distribution is Reed's mechanism itself.
- N5, B = F/v: this is the stationary McKendrick-von Foerster solution (abundance = flux / growth rate). It is the basis of Platt & Denman 1977 [V] and Zhou & Huntley 1997, whose slope is a ratio of intrinsic increase to weight-specific growth [V]. It is also the Kolmogorov flux closure [V].
- N4, the finite-age front: this is a transient of a drift-diffusion with source and is K in spirit (GLLM 2016 [V]).
- Zero-parameter, single-domain tests already exist (Zhang & Sornette 2011; Hisano, Sornette & Mizuno 2011, PRE) [V].
- Blank & Solomon (2000, Physica A 287:279) already showed that a model with a varying number of components gives alpha = 1 over a broad parameter range [V].
- General exponent determination for Markov-modulated multiplicative processes with resets is in Beare & Toda 2022, Econometrica 90(4):1811-1833 [V].
The only remaining contribution is a multi-domain empirical test, which belongs in PRE or a Registered Report, not PRL.
serious_problems: S-1. Much of the prediction is guaranteed by accounting. Because phi = J_R/Q, and Q is the cross-sectional total, the 'prediction' uses the cross-section it is supposed to predict. Under stationarity, phi = (entry rate per unit) × s_e/sbar. The prediction therefore embeds the moment identity behind Gabaix's zeta = 1/(1 - s_min/sbar): a Pareto with zeta near 1 must have sbar/s_e large. F3 ('phi ≈ 0 => zeta ≈ 1') and the zeta-phi association in F7 are close to mathematical consequences of the Pareto family plus the budget. They test stationarity and the gates, not a dynamical selection of zeta = 1. The temporal holdout (R8) does not help: under stationarity the training-window cross-section carries the same information. F2's nulls (zeta ≡ 1; cross-system mean) are too weak. The correct nulls are persistence (each system's own training-window zeta) and a moment null (zeta from the training-window sbar/s_e). The dynamics must add skill over both.

S-2. Lognormal mimicry is a direct alternative, and the proposed shape test lacks power. The size-biased version of a lognormal is again lognormal, so B(u) is a Gaussian in u. It is locally flat at its resource-weighted mode u* = mu_ln + sigma_ln^2: any broad, unimodal resource distribution is locally O_log at its mode [D]. Montroll & Shlesinger (1982, PNAS 79:3380) showed that a broad lognormal is approximately 1/x over a wide range [V]. Perline (2005, Stat. Sci. 20:68-88) showed that truncated lognormal-type samples convincingly mimic power laws ('false inverse power laws') [V]. My simulation (scratchpad referee_ln.py) [D] fits a truncated-Pareto MLE to n = 1600 draws in a window around u*:
- sigma_ln = 5 (e.g. unrelaxed Gibrat with sigma^2*T = 25), ±1 decade: zeta_hat = 0.974 ± 0.027, with 79% of fits within 0.05 of 1.
- sigma_ln = 3.5, ±1 decade: 0.943 ± 0.027.
- The quadratic-curvature LR test (the proposed F5) has power 0.14 at n = 1600 and 0.85 only at n = 16,000 (σ = 5, ±1 dec).
Pure Gibrat with no entry/exit balance, which GLLM 2016 [V] and Schwarzkopf & Farmer 2010 [V] say describes many real systems, therefore produces apparent O_log without the claimed mechanism. The n_tail ≥ 1600 target in E9 is an order of magnitude too small to separate the hypotheses.

S-3. The B5 'local formula' route makes the programme unfalsifiable with respect to O_log. For any stationary one-dimensional Markov diffusion, measured local drift and diffusion determine the stationary density through the zero-flux Fokker-Planck condition. That is all Ioannides & Overman (2003) test. Sending every system that fails the gates (firms, cities, forests) into B5 turns failures of O_log into confirmations of 'stationarity + Markov'. F8 says gate failures do not count as support, but nothing makes them count against generality. This is the formal version of 'deviations are constraints'.

S-4. Gate attrition and statistical power. The systems the authors most care about will fail the gates:
- Firms fail the Gibrat gate: sigma ∝ S^-0.2, so |d ln sigma^2/d ln S| ≈ 0.4 > 0.15 (Stanley 1996; Amaral 1997) [V].
- City growth variance falls with size (Rozenfeld et al. 2008) [V].
- Cities fail the relaxation gate. With sigma about 0.1/yr, m = mu + sigma^2/2 is about 0.005-0.01/yr, so relaxing a log-range of 7-9 takes about 10^3 years [D; the rate values are U].
The likely in-domain set has a handful of systems with phi/m clustered near zero. An errors-in-variables regression on about 5 points with little spread in phi gives a slope CI that includes 1 by default, so F1 cannot fail. zeta_pred - 1 ≈ phi/m is also a ratio of small, noisy rates; when the CI of m approaches 0 its sampling distribution is heavy-tailed, and the delta-method SE in T8 is invalid.

S-5. The primary datasets violate the model's assumptions by construction.
- E2 (GHS-UCDB R2024A): the multitemporal stream exists for 1975-2030 [V]. But urban centres are defined by a density and population threshold, so 'entry' means crossing a definitional threshold, not a birth at the bottom; the design itself concedes such thresholds are not barriers. Earlier-epoch populations are GHS-POP disaggregations of censuses, so the growth variance is partly modelled. Merging centres are coagulation, which violates A2.
- E4 (EDGAR listed firms): entry is an IPO at large size and exit is largely M&A, which is size-dependent. A3 and A2 are violated by design. This is a truncated, selected subsample, not a stock with bottom entry.
- E3 (BDS): the public tables bin firm size into about 12 classes with an open top class '10000+', and firm age includes a 'left censored' class [V]. The tail exponent and the age profile are therefore poorly identified, and firm age is assigned from the oldest establishment [V].
- E6 (fediverse): growth is dominated by exogenous migration shocks, account counts are not conserved (moves, bots, deletions), and a 6-24 month horizon is far shorter than any relaxation time.

S-6. Estimation choices are not defined well enough to stop forking paths.
- Rates: mu, sigma^2 and h can be resource-weighted or unit-weighted. They coincide only if Gibrat holds exactly, which the gates allow to fail by up to 15%.
- Upper truncation: R5 sets an upper front, so a Hill estimator above s_e is biased. The likelihood must be the truncated Pareto (Aban, Meerschaert & Panorska 2006, JASA) [V] or a profile likelihood on B(u).
- Dependence: common shocks within a country or industry break the iid assumption behind SE = zeta/sqrt(n).
- Correlated errors: Q and the tail are both dominated by the same top units, so the errors in phi and zeta_obs are correlated, which the standard errors-in-variables regression does not allow for.
- Scope of the system: 'country' as the system conflicts with Cristelli et al.'s coherence result [V].

S-7. Selection on known outcomes. The candidate systems (US firms 1.06-1.10, CCA cities ≈ 1, Amazee 0.75, administrative places 1.3-1.4) were chosen by people who already know their exponents. Preregistration freezes the analysis but not the knowledge behind the choice of systems. E7 has no sampling frame, its coders are not blinded to the literature, and no inter-rater reliability is reported.

S-8. The mechanism behind the authors' intuition is empirically violated in their flagship systems. 'Nature does not care about concentration' is operationalized as Gibrat's law, yet Gibrat fails measurably for firms (volatility) and cities (variance), and pure Gibrat gives a lognormal, not Zipf (Eeckhout 2004) [V]. When near-Zipf tails appear in these systems, they appear despite the stated mechanism failing. The theory then needs compensating size-dependent drifts it does not predict.
fixable_problems_with_fix: Correct the formal statement. Replace 'O_log <=> phi = 0, a fixed point' with 'zeta -> 1+ as phi/m -> 0+'. Add the budget identity phi = J_R/Q and its consequences: zeta > 1 in every stationary system with positive entry, and the phi < 0 branch lies outside the relaxed class. Rewrite F3/F4 to match.

Add nulls that remove the accounting component. In F2, require skill over (i) persistence, each system's own training-window zeta, and (ii) a moment null, zeta from the training-window sbar/s_e under a Pareto assumption. Report the dynamical predictor's incremental skill over the moment null as the headline number.

Give the prediction dynamical content beyond accounting. Estimate mu, sigma^2 and h from micro growth records on a subpopulation disjoint from the tested cross-section (another region or cohort), or predict transients: the front position after a known founding epoch, or relaxation after a documented shock. Score those transients as primary outcomes.

Fix the estimator. Use a truncated-Pareto or profile-likelihood fit of B(u) on [s_e, front] (Aban et al. 2006), with the front taken from the theory. Use Hill only as a sensitivity analysis. Use a block bootstrap for common shocks, and a joint bootstrap of (phi, m, zeta_obs) to carry their correlated errors into the errors-in-variables regression. Report a Fieller-type or bootstrap CI for phi/m instead of the delta method.

Set the power requirements honestly. Simulate F5 against a lognormal / unrelaxed-Gibrat alternative: about 10^4 tail units per system are needed for ±1-1.5 decade windows (my simulation: power 0.14 at n = 1600, 0.85 at n = 16,000). Preregister a minimum of about 15 gated systems and a minimum spread in phi/m (e.g. a range ≥ 0.2). If these are not met, declare the study uninformative in advance rather than reporting 'no falsification'.

Define the rates once. Fix mu and sigma^2 as resource-weighted moments of incumbent log growth, h as a count hazard, and nu from counts of entrants. Report the unit-weighted alternatives only as sensitivity runs. Freeze s_e and the front formula.

Replace or demote the datasets that violate the assumptions. Move EDGAR to the out-of-domain group, or replace it with an all-firm business register. For cities, use epochs with independent censuses and CCA on raw census grids, and treat mergers as an explicit coagulation term or drop them in a preregistered sensitivity run. Drop the fediverse test, or keep it only as an exploratory analysis.

Give E7 a sampling frame. Draw systems at random from a predefined list (e.g. every dataset in Clauset 2009 and the MetaZipf compilation that has unit-level panels). Have two coders, blind to the exponent, code the sign of phi, and report kappa.

Score B5 systems separately and say what they show. They test 'stationary Markov diffusion', not O_log. Report them in a separate table that cannot contribute to any statement about the generality of zeta = 1.

Rewrite the novelty section. Credit the exact profile to Reed's double-Pareto result (Reed 2001; Reed & Hughes 2002; Reed & Jorgensen 2004 dPlN [U]), the age-size link to Reed's mechanism, flux/speed to McKendrick-von Foerster / Platt-Denman / Silvert-Platt [V listing] / Zhou-Huntley, and general exponent determination to Beare & Toda 2022. Cite Blank & Solomon 2000, Montroll & Shlesinger 1982 and Perline 2005.
what_would_convince_you: A Stage-1-accepted Registered Report in which at least about 15 gated, relaxed systems, drawn from a predefined sampling frame and spanning phi/m from about 0 to at least 0.2, show positive out-of-sample skill over the persistence and moment nulls, with a block-bootstrap CI excluding 0.

Evidence that the prediction is not mechanically implied by the budget: rates measured on a disjoint subpopulation or region predict the held-out cross-section, or the theory correctly predicts transients such as front position and post-shock relaxation that accounting alone cannot give.

A shape test with enough power: at n ≳ 10^4 per system, an exponential B(u) above s_e is preferred to a truncated lognormal (curvature LR test), so that unrelaxed Gibrat and finite-range lognormal mimicry are ruled out.

At least one in-domain system whose predicted zeta is clearly away from 1 (e.g. 1.3 ± 0.05) and is confirmed, together with zeta ≈ 1 appearing only in systems with large m·tau_res. That would show the theory predicts values, not just a clustering near 1.

An explicit full-text comparison showing that N2-N5 are absent from Reed 2001, Reed & Hughes 2002, SMS 2010, Luttmer 2007, GLLM 2016 and Beare & Toda 2022. Otherwise all priority claims should be dropped.

For any claim beyond the Gibrat class, a single resource rule fixed in advance under which a random, unselected sample of systems from several fields has zeta clustering at 1 more tightly than under generic alternatives (lognormal windows, SOC exponents 1/2-2/3). The current evidence goes against this.
referee.strongest_version_you_would_accept: The strongest version I would accept (PRE, or an RSOS Registered Report, not PRL): 'For additive, unit-held stocks whose units grow multiplicatively at size-independent rates, enter near a fixed scale s_e and exit at a size-independent hazard, the stationary resource-per-log-size profile above s_e is exactly exponential, with slope -(zeta - 1). This is the double-Pareto result of Reed (2001) and Saichev, Malevergne and Sornette (2010). The budget forces phi = J_R/Q > 0, so zeta - 1 ≈ phi/m = 1/(m·tau_res), where tau_res is the mean residence time of a resource unit and m its log-speed. Equal resource per logarithmic size (zeta = 1, orthopolity) is therefore the lower limit approached by long-lived, slow-turnover systems, not a fixed point and not a general property. We test this out of sample in N preregistered systems and show that measured rates predict zeta better than persistence and moment-based nulls. Outside this class (events, cascades, size-structured food webs, forests), the same transport identity predicts non-unit exponents, as observed.' 'Orthopolity' may appear as the name of this lower limit together with the accounting identity O_mu and the vacuity lemma. Words such as 'law', 'universal' and 'nature does not care' should not appear. The verified counterexamples (seismic moment, flare energy, IMF, galaxy stellar mass, wildfires, cascades) should be reported with the same prominence as any confirmation.
prior_art_the_authors_missed: Reed's double-Pareto distribution. A GBM observed at an exponentially distributed time has an exact piecewise power-law density whose exponents are roots of the same quadratic. This pre-empts N2 (the exact profile) and N3 (the age-size link). The design cites Reed 2001 only for the exponent equation. Reed, W.J. (2001) Econ. Lett. 74(1):15-19 [V via secondary sources]. https://ideas.repec.org/r/eee/ecolet/v74y2001i1p15-19.html

Reed, W.J. & Hughes, B.D. (2002) From gene families and genera to incomes and internet file sizes: why power laws are so common in nature. PRE 66:067103. It states the general 'killed or observed exponential growth' mechanism across domains, which is the cross-domain claim already made [V]. https://web.uvic.ca/~math-statistics/emeritus/wjreed/PREpowerlaws.pdf

Blank, A. & Solomon, S. (2000) Power laws in cities population, financial markets and internet sites. Physica A 287:279-288. A model with a varying number of components gives alpha = 1 over a broad parameter range, while a fixed number of components with a fixed minimum does not [V]. https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0003240

Montroll, E.W. & Shlesinger, M.F. (1982) On 1/f noise and other distributions with long tails. PNAS 79(10):3380-3383. A broad lognormal is approximately 1/x over a wide range; applied to the size-biased distribution, this gives approximate O_log without any allocation principle [V]. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC346419

Perline, R. (2005) Strong, weak and false inverse power laws. Statistical Science 20(1):68-88, doi:10.1214/088342304000000215. Truncated samples from lognormal-type distributions mimic power laws, and Perline argues many Zipf examples are 'false' power laws [V]. https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ss/1118065043

Mitzenmacher, M. (2004) A brief history of generative models for power law and lognormal distributions. Internet Mathematics 1(2):226-251. It covers the close link between lognormal and power-law generative models [V; whether it discusses double Pareto is U].

Beare, B.K. & Toda, A.A. (2022) Determination of Pareto exponents in economic models driven by Markov multiplicative processes. Econometrica 90(4):1811-1833, doi:10.3982/ECTA17984. This is the general exponent theory with resets and type switching that B5 would need [V].

Aban, I.B., Meerschaert, M.M. & Panorska, A.K. (2006) Parameter estimation for the truncated Pareto distribution. JASA 101:270-277, doi:10.1198/016214505000000411. It is the correct estimator when R5 imposes an upper front [V].

Silvert, W. & Platt, T. (1980) Dynamic energy-flow model of the particle size distribution in pelagic ecosystems. In Kerfoot (ed.), Evolution and Ecology of Zooplankton Communities, pp. 754-763. It is dynamic flux/speed prior art for N5 [V bibliographic listing only]. Also Zhou & Huntley 1997 MEPS 159:61-73, where the steady-state slope is the ratio of intrinsic increase to weight-specific growth [V].

Reed, W.J. & Jorgensen, M. (2004) The double Pareto-lognormal distribution. Communications in Statistics: Theory and Methods 33:1733-1753. It adds a lognormal initial spread to the double Pareto, which is exactly the 'entry spread below s_e' case [U, from memory].

checks.claim: Gabaix (1999), 'Zipf's law for cities: an explanation', QJE 114(3):739-767. If units follow proportional (Gibrat) growth with common mean and variance, and normalized sizes reach a steady state, the upper tail converges to Zipf (zeta = 1). Reading this as 'nature doesn't care' = Gibrat, with normalization by the total.
checks.source: IDEAS/RePEc record https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/qjecon/v114y1999i3p739-767..html; Gabaix PDF https://scholar.harvard.edu/sites/scholar.harvard.edu/files/xgabaix/files/zipfs_law.pdf (search extract); Gabaix 14.13 lecture notes https://ocw.iti.hr/courses/economics/14-13-economics-and-psychology-spring-2004/lecture-notes/1413_lecture24.pdf (normalized multipliers with E[gamma]=1 give Zipf). Secondary sources confirm the lower reflecting barrier and the need for <ln eta> < 0, without which the result is lognormal. Search extracts only; full text not fetched (WebFetch DNS-blocked).

checks.claim: Gabaix reflecting-floor formula zeta = 1/(1 - s_min/s̄), with zeta -> 1+ as s_min/s̄ -> 0, attributed to Gabaix (1999) and marked [V] in the paper design.
checks.source: Not found in any retrievable Gabaix text (QJE 1999; Annual Review of Economics 2009, 1:255-294). The same form appears elsewhere: zeta = 1/(1 - pi), with pi the floor friction on size normalized by the average, in Rozenfeld, Rybski, Gabaix & Makse (2011) AER 101(5):2205-2225 (arXiv:1001.5289); and alpha = 1/(1 - c) in the Levy-Solomon line (review arXiv:adap-org/9912002; arXiv:cond-mat/0102423, which cites Malcai et al. 1999).
checks.correction: The formula follows exactly from a pure Pareto tail above a floor at fixed mean. Until the barrier section of Gabaix (1999) is read, cite it as that identity (e.g., Rozenfeld et al. 2011 or Levy & Solomon) and not as a printed Gabaix result. Malcai, Biham & Solomon (1999, PRE 60:1299) give their own finite-N exponent (their eq. 18) with c entering through its logarithm. So 1/(1 - c) is the idealized N -> infinity pure-Pareto limit, not their exact result.

checks.claim: Malevergne, Saichev & Sornette (2013), JEDC 37(6):1195-1212 (arXiv:1012.0199). Zipf holds exactly under the balance condition mu - h = d + c0: incumbent growth net of exits equals growth of investment in entrants (growth of entrant size c0 plus growth of the number of entrants d). They call Zipf 'the signature of the long-term optimal allocation of resources' / maximum sustainable growth.
checks.source: Conclusion and abstract extracts of arXiv:1012.0199 https://arxiv.org/pdf/1012.0199 and HAL https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-02313060 (Zipf exactly when d + c0 = mu - h; parameters mu, h, c0, d as described). Product-market companion arXiv:1101.5888 treats r = h as the c0 = d = 0 case.
checks.correction: Two caveats from the same paper bear on F3/F7. (1) Zipf is recovered approximately when growth volatility is very large, even if the balance condition fails. (2) A deviation from balance can be approximately compensated by the finite age of the economy. A Physica A follow-up also reports precise Zipf without balanced growth in young systems with strong noise.
